title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US markets closed today for Labor Day; Friday's close stands as the latest print (Dow 53,414.25, S&P 500 7,718.60, Nasdaq 26,507), all down on hot jobs data. Next session opens Tuesday.
Markets: Asia-Pacific trading higher overnight — Nikkei +~2%, Kospi +3.65% — while Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped ~1%.
Markets: Oil surging toward $100/barrel (WTI ~$92, Brent ~$97) and diesel futures at record highs on Middle East supply fears; wheat prices also spiking.

Macro/Policy: US struck three Iranian oil tankers after warships were reportedly targeted with ballistic missiles; Iran vows retaliation, stoking fears of a broader Strait of Hormuz disruption (~20-30% of global seaborne oil), though early diplomatic signals are capping further price gains.
Macro/Policy: Fed rate-hike odds for the Sept 15-16 meeting hold near 58% after Friday's blowout August payrolls report (+162K vs +55K expected); unemployment steady at 4.1%.
Companies: Aon nearing close of a $17B acquisition of USI Insurance from KKR.
